rv.q: It nonetheless comes with an enormous gut-punch, and is all that theatre should strive to be.
Ibrahim’s writing works on your nerves as much as your mind, constantly wrong-footing, confronting and shocking.
Omran’s firebrand lead performance is something to behold.

Sami Ibrahim’s unrestrained and unwieldy script – which won the Theatre Uncut Political Playwriting Award in 2019 – is cluttered with compelling yet underdeveloped threads, ghostly metaphors, and awkward jokes clustered around a familiar story about the futility of violence.
As it is, ‘Two Palestinians Go Dogging’ feels like a lengthy brainstorming session on how to write a great original play about Palestine, rather than a great original play about Palestine.
But lasting nearly three hours and divided into episodic chapters, the show is also simply too long for its own good.
The show is a mess and a bore but it has also lodged in my brain like a nagging earworm.
The overall whole hangs together surprisingly well.
This play may be a metaphor but, when not being shouted at, its bleak picture of the current situation continuing into the future, perhaps getting even worse, can be very moving.
This story is rather interesting and the action scenes are extremely well-presented, but the rest of the play is framed in a Brechtian style.
This crazy sci-fi twist makes everything daft and weightless.
I reflect on an entertaining evening that tackled difficult subject matter with deft humour and inventive staging.

cn.t: Ibrahim's provocative play divides critics with its bold, absurdist take on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Most praise its dark humor and originality, though some find it unfocused or grating, with debate over whether its irreverence illuminates or obscures.
